record.paper_title: Geometric curvature energies: facts, trends, and open problems
record.original_question: For geometric curvature energies on nonsmooth sets in arbitrary dimension, can Meurer’s rectifiability theorem be extended from his integrand KM to the integrands used here for integral Menger curvature or to tangent-point energies, and if so on what suitably broad class of nonsmooth sets? The authors also ask how Meurer’s rectifiability result is related to other recent rectifiability criteria.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k,n\in\mathbb{N}$ with $1\le k<n$, and let $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a Borel set of locally finite $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^k$. For a $(k+2)$-tuple $T=(x_0,\dots,x_{k+1})$ of points in $\mathbb{R}^n$ regarded as a $(k+1)$-simplex, define Meurer's integrand
\[
K_M(T):=\frac{\mathcal{H}^{k+1}(T)}{(\mathrm{diam}\,T)^{k+2}},
\]
where $\mathcal{H}^{k+1}(T)$ is the $(k+1)$-dimensional volume of the simplex with vertices $x_0,\dots,x_{k+1}$. Meurer's theorem asserts: if $\Sigma$ is a $k$-dimensional Borel set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with positive lower $k$-density $\mathcal{H}^k$-almost everywhere and such that
\[
\int_{\Sigma^{k+2}} K_M(x_0,\dots,x_{k+1})^p \, d\mathcal{H}^k(x_0)\cdots d\mathcal{H}^k(x_{k+1}) < \infty
\]
for some sufficiently large $p$, then $\Sigma$ is countably $k$-rectifiable.

Consider the following two alternative integrands defined on $(k+2)$-tuples of points of $\Sigma$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] An integral Menger-type integrand of the form
\[
K_{\mathrm{IM}}(x_0,\dots,x_{k+1}):=\frac{\mathcal{H}^{k+1}(\mathrm{simplex}(x_0,\dots,x_{k+1}))}{\prod_{0\le i<j\le k+1}|x_i-x_j|^{\alpha_{ij}}},
\]
with exponents $\alpha_{ij}\ge 0$ chosen so that the integrand has the natural homogeneity of $k$-dimensional integral Menger curvature.
\item[(b)] A tangent-point integrand: for $x,y\in\Sigma$ with an approximate $k$-plane $T_x\Sigma$ at $x$,
\[
\frac{1}{r_{\mathrm{tp}}(x,y)^q}, \qquad r_{\mathrm{tp}}(x,y):=\frac{|x-y|^2}{2\,\mathrm{dist}(y,x+T_x\Sigma)},
\]
for $q$ in the natural range.
\end{enumerate}

\textbf{Question.} Identify a class $\mathcal{C}$ of $k$-dimensional Borel (``nonsmooth'') sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$, as broad as possible, such that the analogue of Meurer's rectifiability theorem holds with $K_M$ replaced by the integrand $K_{\mathrm{IM}}$ in (a) or by the tangent-point integrand in (b): namely, every $\Sigma\in\mathcal{C}$ with finite corresponding integral energy is countably $k$-rectifiable. Furthermore, clarify the relationship between Meurer's rectifiability criterion and other rectifiability criteria (such as those based on $\beta$-numbers, square functions, or density assumptions).
artifact.status_search_result: A search did not turn up a published result that fully resolves the extension of Meurer's rectifiability theorem from his simplex integrand $K_M$ to the integral Menger curvature integrand or to tangent-point energies on a wide class of nonsmooth $k$-dimensional sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Partial results exist (e.g., Meurer's own theorem on $n$-dimensional Borel sets in $\mathbb{R}^N$ with finite integral Menger curvature, and results above the scale-invariance regime for admissible sets), but a definitive answer for the integrands and the broader nonsmooth-set classes asked about, together with a precise comparison to other modern rectifiability criteria, was not located.

status_evidence.title: Integral Menger Curvature and Rectifiability of n-dimensional Borel sets in Euclidean N-space
status_evidence.snippet: An n-dimensional Borel set in Euclidean N-space with finite integral Menger curvature is n-rectifiable.
status_evidence.claim: Meurer's rectifiability theorem is established for his simplex integrand on n-dimensional Borel sets; extensions to the integral Menger curvature and tangent-point integrands on broad nonsmooth classes are not stated.

status_evidence.title: Rectifiability; a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of rectifiability criteria including tangent and density-based approaches.
status_evidence.claim: Modern rectifiability criteria coexist with Meurer's, but the precise relationship and an extension of his theorem to Menger/tangent-point integrands on general nonsmooth sets is not settled in the surveyed literature.
